question: Who had more impact on the court: Michael Jordan in 1990-91 or LeBron James in 2014-15?
answer:
# On-Court Impact Review

## Answer

**My judgement: I lean toward Michael Jordan.**

**Criterion:** observed on-court production across scoring efficiency, defensive event generation, and postseason performance under an observed-contribution lens

**Decisive reason:** Michael Jordan generated superior scoring volume and efficiency in both the regular season and playoffs, backed by higher defensive activity proxies in steals and blocks. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)

**Strongest counterargument:** The opposing player registered higher regular season assist volume and defensive rebounding counts, reflecting greater perimeter creation and board-securing responsibilities. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)

**Why this judgement:** While the right player held an advantage in assist volume, the left player maintained superior assist-to-turnover security alongside a massive scoring and efficiency edge.

**What could change it:** This preference could be reversed if team context and raw assist generation were weighted above individual scoring efficiency and defensive event metrics.

## Dimension findings

- **Offense and era:** Michael Jordan leads the selected measures across the requested phases.
- **Playmaking and ball security:** The indicators disagree; one player does not dominate all selected measures.
- **Defensive evidence:** Regular Season: Michael Jordan has the higher steals per 36 minutes; Regular Season: Michael Jordan has the higher blocks per 36 minutes; Regular Season: LeBron James has the higher defensive rebounds per 36 minutes; Playoffs: Michael Jordan has the higher steals per 36 minutes; Playoffs: Michael Jordan has the higher blocks per 36 minutes; Playoffs: LeBron James has the higher defensive rebounds per 36 minutes. Activity indicators do not settle individual defense.
- **Team on/off context:** Regular Season: no single comparable pair; missing or multiple team stints prevent a summary ranking; Playoffs: no single comparable pair; missing or multiple team stints prevent a summary ranking. This describes team association, not an isolated player effect.

This position compares observed contributions, not innate ability. Offensive judgement uses PPG and TS; league-relative efficiency is a separate cross-era check. Playmaking uses assists per minute and assists/turnovers, not a complete model of creation. Defensive activity cannot settle individual defense. Team on/off is association rather than causation.

**Scope:** 1990-91–1990-91 versus 2014-15–2014-15; Regular Season, Playoffs.

## Key evidence

- **Offense and era / Regular Season:** Michael Jordan (1990): Points per game **31.46** per game, True shooting **60.5** %; LeBron James (2014): Points per game **25.26** per game, True shooting **57.66** %. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- **Playmaking and ball security / Playoffs:** Michael Jordan (1990): Assists per 36 minutes **7.42** per 36 minutes, Assists per turnover **3.3** ratio; LeBron James (2014): Assists per 36 minutes **7.21** per 36 minutes, Assists per turnover **2.06** ratio. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- **Defensive evidence / Regular Season:** Michael Jordan (1990): Steals per 36 minutes **2.65** per 36 minutes, Blocks per 36 minutes **0.98** per 36 minutes, Defensive rebounds per 36 minutes **4.44** per 36 minutes; LeBron James (2014): Steals per 36 minutes **1.57** per 36 minutes, Blocks per 36 minutes **0.71** per 36 minutes, Defensive rebounds per 36 minutes **5.27** per 36 minutes. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- **Team on/off context / Regular Season:** Michael Jordan: comparable evidence unavailable; LeBron James (2014 / Cleveland Cavaliers): On-minus-off net rating **16.7** points / 100 possessions, ON min **2,493** minutes, OFF min **1,463** minutes. - **Finding:** LeBron James has higher playoff PPG but lower TS. Check minutes, attempts and per-minute production before interpreting more points as broad improvement. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- **Follow-up: Completed.** Matched minutes, attempts and per-minute scoring are shown below. More PPG alone does not establish broader improvement.
- **What the follow-up changes:** LeBron James has higher playoff PPG but lower shooting efficiency. Minutes/game changed from 36.13 to 42.2, attempts/game from 18.54 to 27.2, and points/36 minutes from 25.17 to 25.64. This separates additional playing/shot opportunity from efficiency; higher PPG is not an across-the-board improvement.
